messages:
anya: Heads up — console shows canary at ~12% traffic for service=router-api even though rollout is set to 1%.
anya: Noticed this after the XFH header normalization change rolled yesterday.
deploy-bot: deployment notice: canary=router-api:canary-2026-03-15 by @sam at 1987654300
sam: ugh. can you paste the observed splits from the console?
anya: Screenshot pasted but gist: routes: { default: 99, canary: 1 } but traffic graph spikes to ~12% over last hour.
lucas: quick theory: hash key includes normalized host header. after the change some hosts are being rewritten (strip port) causing different buckets across proxies => sticky sessions break.
maria: if header normalization flips host for some requests, the hash(seed) changes. with our fallback policy (missing header -> client_ip) requests could end up on canary more frequently.
kai: can you dump an example request? any logs showing computed bucket/hmac?
anya: pasted logs:
```
WARN routing: computed-bucket=canary seed=0x7fa3b3 host="api.internal:443" normalized_host="api.internal" hash=0x2f3a req_id=abc123
WARN routing: computed-bucket=default seed=0x7fa3b3 host="api.internal" normalized_host="api.internal" hash=0x1a9c req_id=def456
```
anya: note the first line has host with port before normalization; second doesn't. hash differs.
sam: that explains flips but not steady 12% — we'd expect jitter, not sustained bias. maybe some proxies still send pre-normalized header consistently for a subset of clients.
lucas: also check guard evaluation order. if header-based split rule runs before sticky cookie check, fallback path could pick a different key. config snippet from console: 
```
policy:
  - guard: header("x-forwarded-host")
    split: { canary: 0.01, default: 0.99 }
  - guard: cookie("_rid")
    sticky: true
```
lucas: that ordering will run header guard first which may bypass cookie sticky if header present. if some frontends add X-Forwarded-Host inconsistently, cookie stickiness won't apply.
maria: @sam can we rollback the normalization or change guard order to ensure cookie sticky runs first?
sam: quick mitigation: flip guard order in console, set header guard to a secondary rule. doing a canary change to policy-config now.
sam: also adding a telemetry probe to log which key was used for hashing (host|cookie|ip) and the resulting bucket for a sample of requests.
deploy-bot: config change applied to policy router-api @ 1987654380 by sam (dry-run=false)
anya: after flip, early numbers show canary back down to ~1.2% (still a bit noisy). keeping an eye.
kai: follow-up action items: 1) add explicit normalization test for X-Forwarded-Host in e2e; 2) modify rollout UX to warn if header-based guards exist ahead of sticky guards; 3) add metric split.leak.routed_by_header.
sam: agreed. filing a quick ticket for the UX warning and e2e test. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
